compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`infra/terraform/user_data.sh` protects gate scratch with a two-marker scheme, and its own comment
states the contract:

    #   .gate-scratch-required — beside the mount point, on ROOT: the DECLARATION that
    #     this host has a dedicated scratch volume. Survives an unmount.
    #   .gate-scratch-mounted  — inside the mount point, on the VOLUME: the PROOF.
    #     Disappears with the volume.
    # Declaration present + proof absent => gate admission refuses instead of quietly
    # repopulating the store on root.

    touch "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/../.gate-scratch-required"
    touch "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/.gate-scratch-mounted"

Both `touch`es run only AFTER a successful mount, inside `user_data.sh`, which executes **once, at
instance launch**. So the DECLARATION — the thing that arms the refusal — can only be written by the
same one-shot path that performs the mount.

A volume attached to an ALREADY-RUNNING instance therefore produces neither marker. Gate admission
then observes "no declaration", concludes this host has no dedicated scratch volume, and proceeds on
root. Silently.

## The three states, and the one that is undefended

| declaration | proof | meaning | behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| present | present | mounted and healthy | proceed. Correct. |
| present | absent | volume vanished after being provisioned | REFUSE. Correct — the case the design was built for. |
| **absent** | absent | **host has the volume in AWS but does not know it** | **proceed on root, no complaint** |

The design distinguishes three states and defends against one. The third is not a rare edge: it is
the guaranteed outcome of the ordinary operational sequence "Terraform attaches a volume to a running
instance".

## Confirmed live on the production host, 2026-09-05 ~11:55 UTC

    $ mountpoint /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
    /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch is not a mountpoint

    $ ls -la /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required
    ls: cannot access '/var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required': No such file or directory

    $ ls /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/
    rebar-gate-snapshots   reviewbot-vnaa57x_   semgrep-mcp   tmpgvy_yxuz   tmpqk2k1l2n.json

    $ lsblk
    nvme2n1   50G   (no fstype)      <- the gate-scratch volume: attached, raw, unmounted

So gate snapshots, a live review-bot clone and semgrep-mcp are all writing to the ROOT filesystem
right now — the exact condition ADR 0112 provisioned this volume to end — and nothing anywhere is
raising a word about it.

## Why this is its own bug and not just `dcc3`

`dcc3` is "mount the volume": a one-host remediation. This ticket is the reason the miss was SILENT
rather than loud, and it recurs on every future host that acquires the volume after launch —
including any replacement instance where Terraform attaches before user_data reaches its mount block,
and any future volume added by the same pattern. Mounting the volume on this host closes `dcc3` and
leaves this defect entirely intact.

It is also a specific instance of a pattern this repo keeps finding: a guard whose PRECONDITION is
written by the very path that was skipped, so the guard cannot fire about its own absence. Compare
`affd-913c-3fb0-40fb`, where a cross-cutting contract lived only inside a revertable commit and
nothing detected its loss.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The declaration is derivable from state that survives a post-launch volume attach — for example
      the Terraform-known volume id rendered into a config the host reads, or a systemd unit that
      reconciles markers on boot — so that "the volume exists in AWS" and "the host knows it should
      have one" cannot diverge. State which source was chosen and why it cannot be skipped.
- [ ] The undefended state is made loud: with the volume attached and unmounted and NO declaration
      present, gate admission refuses (or an alarm fires) rather than proceeding on root. Proven by a
      test that constructs exactly that state.
- [ ] Defect-seeded: remove whatever new mechanism arms the declaration and confirm a test turns RED.
      A guard never observed failing is not evidence.
- [ ] The existing two-state behaviour is unchanged — declaration+proof still proceeds, and
      declaration-without-proof still refuses. Both pinned by tests so this change cannot silently
      relax the case that already worked.
- [ ] Arming order is safe: the declaration must never be written on a host that cannot yet satisfy
      it, or every gate on that box blocks. State explicitly where in the sequence it is written and
      why that point is correct.
- [ ] Portability: host config + systemd + local tests; no CI-provider trigger.

## Testing

1. RED first: construct the absent/absent state and assert gate admission refuses. On current `main`
   it proceeds, so the test fails for the right reason.
2. Confirm present/absent still refuses and present/present still proceeds — the regression guard.
3. Confirm the arming path cannot fire before a successful mount, so a partially-provisioned host is
   not bricked by its own declaration.

## Provenance

Found while inspecting the host for `dcc3` (`dcc3-75ee-26ce-4840`), where the full measurement is
recorded. `dcc3` remains the "mount this host's volume" remediation; this ticket is why the gap was
invisible.
compiled_state.title: The gate-scratch refusal can only arm itself at instance launch, so a volume attached to a running host lands in a silent third state the guard was never designed to see
